without.degraded: Lakana works, but slower than usual.
without.down: Lakana cannot get work done right now. Tell an administrator.

causes.database: The database cannot be reached, so nothing gets done. Check that the database runs, then read the server’s log.
causes.storage: The object storage cannot be reached, so tables cannot be read or written. Check that it runs and that the server may reach it.
causes.no_worker: No worker is running, so queries and jobs wait until one starts.
causes.worker_lost_one: Queries are slower: {{count}} of {{total}} workers is down.
causes.worker_lost_other: Queries are slower: {{count}} of {{total}} workers are down.
causes.memory_high: The workers are close to their memory limit, so a large query may be stopped.

recent.title: Recently opened
recent.none: Nothing opened yet. The tables you open will show here; queries, jobs and runs follow once their pages arrive in a later release.
recent.toCatalog: Find a table in the Catalog

work.title: Your work
work.none: Nothing yet: the repositories you connect or deploy, and their jobs, show here.

ended.idle: Your session ended after a time without activity. Sign in again.
ended.lifetime: Your session reached its maximum length and ended. Sign in again.
ended.sign_out_everywhere: You signed out on every device.
ended.ended_by_admin: An administrator ended your session. Sign in again.
ended.replaced: A newer sign-in in this browser replaced this session. Sign in again.
ended.deactivated: Your account is deactivated, so your session ended. Ask an administrator to reactivate it, then sign in again.
ended.token_revoked: The token this session was created with was revoked or expired, so the session ended. Sign in again.
ended.recovery: Your account was recovered with a recovery link, which ended every earlier session. Sign in again with your new passkey.
ended.passkey_copied: A copy of one of your passkeys was detected; it is disabled and every session of your account was ended. Sign in with another passkey, or ask an administrator for a recovery link.
ended.passkey_removed: An administrator removed one of your passkeys, which ended your sessions. Sign in again with another passkey, or ask an administrator for a recovery link.
ended.reactivated: Your account was reactivated, which ended every earlier session and removed its passkeys. Ask the server operator for a new sign-in link.

errors.unreachable: Lakana could not be reached. Check that the server is running and your network works, then try again.
errors.unexpected: Something went wrong in the interface. Reload the page and try again.

passkey.cancelled: The passkey request was cancelled or took too long. Try again when you are ready.
passkey.unsupported: This browser cannot use passkeys. Use a current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
passkey.duplicate: This browser or password manager already holds a passkey for this account. To add another, choose a different place in the browser's window, such as a phone or tablet or a security key; or sign in with the passkey you have.
passkey.wrongAddress: Passkeys work only at the address Lakana was set up with. Open Lakana at that address and try again.
passkey.failed: The browser could not use the passkey ({{name}}). Try again, or use another device.

signIn.title: Sign in to Lakana
signIn.intro: Sign in with your passkey: your fingerprint, face, PIN or security key.
signIn.refused: This passkey did not sign you in: it may belong to another Lakana server, or it was removed. Try another passkey, or ask an administrator for a recovery link.
signIn.noPasskey: No passkey on this device? Ask an administrator for a recovery link.

link.signInIntro: This link signs you in once. Continue only if you asked for it.
link.joinIntro: This invitation creates your account. Continue only if you expected it.

used.title: This link was already used
used.body: Each sign-in link works once. Sign in with your passkey, or ask whoever sent the link for a new one.

expired.title: This link has expired
expired.body: Ask whoever sent it for a new link, or sign in with your passkey.

withdrawn.title: This link was withdrawn
withdrawn.body: Ask whoever sent it for a new link, or sign in with your passkey.

unknown.title: This link does not work
unknown.body: Check that you opened all of it, including everything after #, or ask whoever sent it for a new link.

link.replaces: This browser is signed in as {{name}}; continuing signs that session out.

addPasskey.title: Add a passkey
addPasskey.required: You signed in with a link that works once. Add a passkey now: from then on it signs you in with your fingerprint, face, PIN or security key.
addPasskey.offer: Sign in faster next time: add a passkey, and this device signs you in with your fingerprint, face, PIN or security key. You can also add one later.

notices.label: Sign-in notices
notices.dismissFailed: The notice could not be dismissed: {{detail}}

recovery_used.self: A recovery link was used on your account on {{date}}. If this was not you, tell an administrator at once.
recovery_used.other: A recovery link was used on the account of {{subject}} on {{date}}.

passkey_disabled.self: One of your passkeys was disabled on {{date}} because a copy of it was detected. Sign in with another passkey, or ask an administrator for a recovery link, and tell an administrator if you did not copy it.
passkey_disabled.other: A passkey of {{subject}} was disabled on {{date}} because a copy of it was detected.

passkey_added.self: A passkey was added to your account on {{date}}. If this was not you, tell an administrator at once.
passkey_added.other: A passkey was added to the account of {{subject}} on {{date}}.

other.self: Something changed about signing in to your account on {{date}}.
other.other: Something changed about signing in to the account of {{subject}} on {{date}}.

copy.select: Select the line and copy it.

catalog.healthMore: {{word}}, and {{count}} more, listed on the table page
catalog.noHitsHint: Search looks at table and column names, labels and descriptions. Try a shorter text.

unknown.environment: There is no environment named {{environment}} that you may read.
unknown.namespace: There is no namespace {{namespace}} in {{environment}} that you may read.

catalog.noEnvironment: You may read no environment yet. Ask an administrator for access.

result.capped: The search stopped after {{count, number}} tables. Use a longer text or choose a namespace.

empty.text: No tables in {{place}} yet. Tables appear once a project is deployed.

people.capped: Showing the first {{count}}. Type part of a name to find someone who is not listed.
people.serviceNote: {{name}} is a service account: it signs in with its API token, not a passkey, so it needs no recovery link. Issue it a new token instead.

invites.intro: An invite is a link that creates a person's account, with no rights, the first time it is used. It works once, for 7 days.
invites.none: No invite is open. Invite someone with the button above, or from the command line:
invites.name: Name
invites.nameHelp: The name the person signs in as; it must not be taken, in any letter case.
invites.displayNameHelp: How Lakana shows the person, such as their full name.
invites.shownOnce: It works once, until {{date}}. This is the only time Lakana shows it: copy it now and send it to {{name}} yourself.
invites.confirm: The link creates the account with no rights. Before you grant any role, confirm outside Lakana that the person who signed up is {{name}}: ask them in person, by phone or in your team chat.

recovery.intro: A recovery link lets a person who lost their passkeys back in. It works once, for 1 hour; using it replaces their passkeys, ends their sessions and tells every administrator.
recovery.none: No recovery link is open. Issue one with the button above when someone has lost their passkeys.
recovery.confirmFirst: Issue one only after confirming outside Lakana, in person or by phone, that the person asked for it.
recovery.shownOnce: It works once, for 1 hour, until {{date}}. Using it removes the passkeys of {{name}}, ends their sessions and tells every administrator. This is the only time Lakana shows it: copy it now and send it to {{name}} yourself.
recovery.operatorOnly: Only the server operator can recover an administrator: run this where the server runs, with the bootstrap token.
recovery.operatorFor: {{name}} is an administrator, so only the server operator can recover this account: run this where the server runs, with the bootstrap token.
recovery.operatorForYou: If you lose every passkey, only the server operator can let you back in, because you are an administrator: they run this where the server runs, with the bootstrap token. Add a second passkey before you need it.

account.title: Passkeys and sessions
account.purpose: Your passkeys sign you in; your sessions are the browsers you are signed in on.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.none: You have no passkey yet. Add one: it signs you in with your fingerprint, face, PIN or security key.
passkeys.disabled: Disabled: a copy of it was detected
passkeys.elsewhere: Not usable at this address: it was added while Lakana had another address
passkeys.ownEffect: It no longer signs you in. Your other passkeys keep working; Lakana does not remove your last working one.
passkeys.otherEffect: {{person}} is signed out everywhere and needs another passkey to sign in. If it was their only one, they need a recovery link, and for an administrator only the server operator can let them back in.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.effect: {{name}} is signed out in every browser and signs in again with a passkey.

status.intro: The instance in detail: each worker with its work and memory, and why the instance is degraded or down.

signIn.intro: How long a browser session lasts. API tokens are not affected. Saving asks for a passkey touch when yours is older than 15 minutes.
signIn.idleHelp: A session ends after this long without anything the person did. Between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes ({{minText}} to {{maxText}}).
signIn.absoluteHelp: A session ends after this long, however active the person is. Between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes ({{minText}} to {{maxText}}).
signIn.appliesLater: A change applies to sessions that begin afterwards; open sessions keep their lengths.
signIn.saved: Saved. New sessions use these lengths.
signIn.idleOutOfBounds: The idle timeout is between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes. Enter a whole number in that range.
signIn.absoluteOutOfBounds: The longest session is between {{min}} and {{max}} minutes. Enter a whole number in that range.
signIn.shorterThanIdle: The longest session cannot be shorter than the idle timeout ({{idle}} minutes). Make it longer, or the idle timeout shorter.

repositories.intro: Lakana deploys jobs from Git repositories and only ever reads from them.

connect.title: Connect a repository
connect.intro: Lakana deploys a project from its Git repository over SSH, with a deploy key it makes for you. Nothing is stored until you confirm the host's keys.

where.heading: 1. The repository
where.urlHelp: The address you clone it with, such as git@github.com:team/analytics.git or https://github.com/team/analytics.
where.name: Name in Lakana
where.nameHelp: Deploys and the command line use it. No dots, slashes, percent signs or spaces.
where.known: A {{host}} repository. Lakana connects to it over SSH: {{url}}
where.other: Lakana connects to it over SSH: {{url}}
where.urlEmpty: Enter the repository's URL, the one you clone it with.
where.urlBad: This is not a repository URL. Enter it as git@host:team/repo.git, ssh://git@host/team/repo.git or https://host/team/repo.
where.httpsOther: Lakana cannot tell this host's SSH address. Enter the SSH URL (the host's Clone button shows it, such as git@host:team/repo.git), or use a token instead.
where.nameEmpty: Enter a name for the repository.
where.nameBad: A name has no dots, slashes, percent signs or spaces. Try {{suggestion}}.
where.queryOrFragment: A repository URL has no '?' or '#'. Copy the address from the host's Clone button.

token.body: Register the HTTPS URL with an access token stored as a secret. A token belongs to a person and expires: when they leave or it runs out, deploys stop. A deploy key belongs to the repository.
token.how: How to store the token and register the repository

keys.heading: 2. Confirm the host's keys
keys.body: A worker fetches the host's SSH keys. Compare each fingerprint with the ones the host publishes, and tick only the keys that match.
keys.waiting: Asking a worker to fetch the keys…
keys.compareOther: Ask the host's administrator for its fingerprints, or find them in the host's documentation.
keys.othersNote: Tick another key type only when you compared its fingerprint too.
keys.found_one: Found {{count}} key of the host. Compare its fingerprint, then tick it if it matches.
keys.found_other: Found {{count}} keys of the host. Compare each fingerprint, then tick the ones that match.
keys.none: The host offered no SSH key. Check that the URL is the SSH address of your Git host, then fetch again.
keys.noWorker: No worker answered within two minutes. Start one (docker compose up -d worker, or lakana server start --local), then try again.

create.heading: 3. Create the repository and its keys
create.body: Lakana registers the repository with the keys you ticked, then makes a key pair for each environment. The private keys stay on the server as secrets; you see only the public keys. This asks for a passkey touch.
create.action: Create the repository and its keys
create.tick: Tick each key that matches, above, first.
create.working: Creating the repository and its keys…
create.notMade: The repository is registered; its keys are not made yet.
create.done: Made keys for {{environments}}. Add each one at your Git host, then test access below.
create.already: {{name}} was already registered with this URL, so Lakana went on to its keys.
create.otherKeys: A repository with this address is already registered with other host keys. Check them with {{show}}. If the keys ticked here are the right ones, save them with {{save}} and run {{update}}.
create.otherKind: A {{kind}} repository with this address is already registered as {{name}}. Check it with {{show}}, or choose another name above.
create.unread: Lakana could not read it to compare. Check it with {{show}}, or choose another name above.
create.conflict: Try again; if it happens again, the server's log has the details.
create.taken: A repository named {{name}} already exists with another URL. Choose another name above.
create.add: Add each key as a read-only deploy key at your Git host.
create.pageOther: At your Git host, open the repository's settings and its deploy keys.
create.readOnly: Keep it read-only: leave write access off. Lakana only reads, and a key that may push could change what your production environment deploys.
create.skipped: No key in {{environments}}: you may not manage secrets there. Someone who may runs lakana repo deploy-key {{name}}.
create.later: An environment created later has no key yet: make one with lakana repo deploy-key {{name}} and add it as an additional deploy key at your Git host; the other environments' keys keep working.

test.heading: 4. Test access
test.body: A worker reads the repository with the key of {{environment}}, as a deploy would. Add that key at your Git host first.
test.waiting: Asking a worker to read the repository…
test.next: Next: deploy it, by hand or from CI.

welcome.title: Welcome to Lakana
welcome.text: Lakana keeps your team’s tables in one place, with the jobs that build them, the checks that guard them and who may read them. Every change comes from your project’s Git repository.
welcome.tour: This short tour shows where things are, one place at a time. You can leave it at any step, and Help brings it back.

home.text: Where every sign-in lands: whether the instance is well, what needs your attention and what you opened recently.

catalog.text: Every table you may read, with its columns, its health and where its data comes from.

queries.text: Write SQL against the tables you may read, and see or download the result.

jobs.text: The jobs your projects deploy and their runs: what ran, what failed and what runs next.

connections.text: The databases and services your project loads its data from.

access.text: Who may sign in, and what each person, group and token may do.

settings.text: The instance’s status, its environments and how this server is set up.

search.text: Press {{keys}} anywhere to go to a place or run a command by typing a few letters.

help.text: Help brings back this tour and Get started, opens the documentation and lists the keyboard shortcuts.

profile.title: Profile picture
profile.intro: A JPEG, PNG or WebP image of up to 5 MB and 40 megapixels. Lakana keeps a square cut from the centre and removes the file's details, such as where a photo was taken.
profile.wrongType: Use a JPEG, PNG or WebP image.
profile.tooLarge: This picture is larger than 5 MB. Choose a smaller JPEG, PNG or WebP image.
profile.stillSending: A picture is still being sent, so this one was not. Choose it again once the first is saved.
profile.removeBody: {{name}} sees their initials instead, and can set a new picture from the menu under their name.
